subject: Request: cohort pilot extension + voucher-to-retainer conversion
messages:
From: Alice Park <alice@launchforge.co>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Anju Rao <anju@venturehub.org>
Date: Wed, 22 Aug 2028 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Request: extend cohort pilot & convert vouchers to retainer

Hi Dylan,

Thanks again for the onboarding support last month — the team has made great progress with the integration. A couple of asks from our side as we move toward demo day: we’re tracking higher-than-expected consumption during model tuning and are likely to exceed our cohort voucher allocation by ~35% over the next three weeks.

Two requests we hope you can consider as an exception for LaunchForge cohort companies:

- A 30-day trial extension (no additional charge) so our team can finish the end-to-end demo without throttling.
- Permission to apply remaining cohort vouchers as a credit against a short-term retainer (we’d like to convert vouchers into a retainer credit to cover the month of Sept while we close seed paperwork).

I’ve attached the usage_report.csv (current token/embedding breakdown) and a short MVP-demo.mp4 for context. If it helps, we can agree to a simple milestone: we convert up to $12,000 of vouchers to a retainer credit if LaunchForge signs a 3-month pilot retainer (month-to-month thereafter) within 30 days.

We know this is non-standard — happy to take whichever path you prefer (partial conversion + extension, or an extension-only). Could you let us know feasibility and any documentation you’d need?

Best,
Alice Park
Head of Programs, LaunchForge
alice@launchforge.co
(415) 555-0189

Attachments: usage_report.csv, MVP-demo.mp4

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Alice Park <alice@launchforge.co>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Aug 2028 16:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: extend cohort pilot & convert vouchers to retainer

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear ask and for sending the usage snapshot. Looping in Ben (pricing) and Marissa (program ops) so we can evaluate an exception quickly.

High level: we can typically accommodate a short extension; conversion of vouchers to cash-equivalent credit is evaluated case-by-case. A couple of operational notes / options I want to propose so we have something concrete to act on:

Option A — Extension + Voucher-to-Credit (preferred)
- Redwood grants 30-day trial extension for LaunchForge cohort account.
- Convert up to $10,000 of remaining cohort vouchers into a one-time invoice credit to be applied to the first month of a signed 3-month retainer (must sign within 30 days).

Option B — Extension + Support Add-on
- 30-day extension plus 2 weeks of prioritized onboarding support at no charge; vouchers remain non-convertible but we provide a usage guardrail to prevent surprise overages.

We’ll need a quick waiver for anything over $10k and Director sign-off for amounts >$15k. Ben — can you confirm whether $10k is workable and what approvals are needed to push to $12k? Marissa — any program constraints (cohort policy) we should flag?

If either option works for you, I’ll draft a short amendment/proposal and share a DocuSign link for signature. Can you confirm whether the milestone you proposed (sign within 30 days) is acceptable?

Thanks — I’ll aim to get an internal decision in 48 hours.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
dylan.brooks@redwood.com

Attachment: proposal-draft.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 24 Aug 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: extend cohort pilot & convert vouchers to retainer

Dylan — quick internal note on approvals and recommended counter:

Thanks for looping us in. Given LaunchForge is a flagship accelerator cohort, I’m comfortable recommending a limited exception with guardrails:

- Approve Option A but cap voucher conversion at $8,000 (net credit). We’ll offer an additional 25% discount on the first month of the retainer if they sign the 3-month pilot within 21 days.
- Require the customer to accept a usage cap clause after the credit is exhausted (automated throttling + email alerts).
- For amounts between $8k–$12k we can escalate to Director (Marissa to get sign-off); anything >$12k needs VP approval.

Operational asks:
- Have the customer sign a short amendment (one page) acknowledging the credit cap, milestone, and usage cap.
- Capture the concession as a HubSpot line item and attach a discount-waiver-form.docx to the deal record (I’ll fill the finance fields).

Marissa — can you confirm program okays a 21-day milestone instead of 30? If yes I’ll prepare the waiver and the DocuSign.

On tone: this is a good relationship play; LaunchForge is high signal for other cohort partners. I prefer the $8k + 25% approach vs stretching to $12k with slower approvals.

Ben Carter
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
